# ethereum-optimism/optimism Monthly Report (May 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
In May 2026, development focused heavily on maturing the **interoperability (interop) stack** and refining the **Superchain** infrastructure. Key milestones included the default enablement of Cannon Kona and L2CM features, alongside the introduction of critical Service Level Indicator (SLI) metrics for the `op-supernode`. While the team made significant strides in streamlining CI processes and resolving genesis sync bugs, efforts were also directed toward troubleshooting a non-deterministic panic in `op-reth` during database upgrades. The month's activity signals a transition toward production readiness for interoperable proofs and decentralized governance migrations.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Interoperability & Supernode Infrastructure
A primary focus this month was enhancing the `op-supernode` and the interoperability framework to meet quality gates for upcoming releases.
*   **SLI Qualification:** New Prometheus metrics were integrated into `op-supernode` to track verification latency and chain-specific measurements (SLI-SN-4 through SLI-SN-8) [#20443](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20443).
*   **Feature Enablement:** Cannon Kona and L2CM are now hardcoded as default paths in the devfeature bitmap for both Go and Solidity, simplifying the integration of these core interop components [#20470](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20470), [#20439](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20439).
*   **Routing & Prestates:** Work began on routing `SuperPermissionedGameType` through `cannon-kona` in `op-challenger` [#20501](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20501).

### Protocol Reliability & Bug Fixes
Several critical fixes were deployed to ensure stable node operations and accurate state transitions.
*   **Genesis Sync:** Resolved a bug in `LightCL` where the L2 genesis block was incorrectly treated as an unset state, preventing proper follow-source initialization [#20385](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20385).
*   **Execution Engine Fixes:** Addressed an `op-reth` initialization stall by ensuring RW transactions are committed before state dump initialization [#20485](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20485).
*   **State Transitions:** A fix for `op-revm` ensures that Bedrock deposits correctly increment nonces upon a Halt [#20504](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20504).

### CI/CD & Developer Experience
The team optimized the development pipeline to reduce resource consumption and improve build speeds.
*   **CI Optimization:** Downsized CI jobs and introduced a new Rust build recipe that excludes example crates to accelerate build times [#20423](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20421).
*   **Testing Improvements:** Enhanced acceptance tests to use preset budgets and improved the `TestSequencer` to drive `AfterChainHead` setups [#20478](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/20482).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **Sync & Dispute Monitoring:** Resolved flaky timeouts in `TestTruncateDatabaseOnELResync` [#19897](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19897). Clarified that `op-dispute-mon` can simultaneously monitor multiple game types (CANNON and SUPER_CANNON_KONA) by utilizing both rollup and supernode RPCs [#20476](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20476).

### New & Active Issues
*   **op-reth Upgrade Panic:** A high-priority issue [#20462](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20462) involves a fatal panic in `StateRootTask` during 1.x to 2.x upgrades. The panic appears to be a non-deterministic assertion failure in the shared trie computation logic.
*   **Contract Migration Concerns:** New issues highlight potential gaps in the `OPContractsManagerMigrator`, specifically regarding the repointing of `delayedWETH` during shared-DGF migrations [#20502](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20502).
*   **Supernode Logic:** A discrepancy was identified where `VerifiedRequiredL1` incorrectly calculates the minimum instead of the maximum of per-chain L1 values [#20481](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/20481).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The month saw active technical coordination regarding the **V700 vs. V800 upgrade path**. Discussions between contributors like @ajsutton and @sbvegan clarified that `SUPER_PERMISSIONED_CANNON` prestate changes should target the V800 template to align with the Interop release (Upgrade 20) [#1412](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/1412). Additionally, community members have stepped up to lead refactoring efforts, such as @NikhilSharmaWe's proposal to deduplicate Engine API validations in the miner logic [#688](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/688).
